Overview We're tackling some of the biggest problems the world faces today, one idea at a time. muru-D is Telstra's hub for incubating ideas, products, and technologies. The name muru-D has a meaningful origin rooted in the Sydney Aboriginal Eora language. The word 'muru' means path, symbolising a journey or direction. The 'D' stands for digital, representing the focus on digital innovation. Together, muru-D signifies a pathway to digital innovation. We explore new technologies and rapidly prototype solutions, drawing on our expertise in 5G, IoT, connectivity, edge computing, and applied AI. Partnering with industry, experts, and universities, we develop real-world solutions for real-world problems. Our
Our process includes prototyping, proof-of-concepts, customer trials, and human-centred design workshops.
We also support founders driving social technological impact and innovation in AI, VR, AR, drones, satellites, and robotics.
We achieve this with our partners and experts through iterative prototyping, POCs, customer trials, and the Labs Application Testing Environment to achieve market readiness.
Support more start-ups through their growth journeys We aim to accelerate, support and grow our start-up portfolio – which includes over 80 start-ups across Australia, Asia, and USA.

Fibre sen﻿sing We’ve turned existing optical fibre runs into continuous passive acoustic sensors, implementing AI and Machine Learning on the sensor data to generate a range of composition statistics.
Agritech We've invested in the Agritech industry, including through active trials and Commonwealth grant participation with Zetifi and Farmbot.
Autonomous robotics We test different robotics platforms such as Unitree, investigate how our network can be the conduit to enable autonomous mining and workplace of the future use cases.
Apple Vision Pro We develop applications using the visionOS ecosystem, such as testing how residential wireless coverage can be enhanced with augmented reality.

Wiliot Bluetooth tracking In collaboration with a global IoT solution provider specialising in battery-less Bluetooth tagging technology, we are showcasing the most advanced innovations in asset tracking.
We commit to working together to build a prosperous and inclusive Australia .

Make sure you understand what the grant program is looking for and what you need to provide.

How to find and apply for small business grants – Telstra Publisher: Telstra Name: How to find and apply for small business grants – Telstra Copyrighted By: Telstra Family Friendly: Yes Language: English Skip to main content Telstra Personal Home Page Search Telstra Telstra Search Telstra Telstra Search Telstra Telstra Personal Business Enterprise Search Telstra Language Sign in Telstra Smarter Business Planning and strategy How to find and apply for small business grants Run a small business? You could be eligible for support. Learn how to find and apply for grants and funding programs, from government to start-up grants. 24 March 2022 · 6 minute read How can funding help my business? It may seem like we’re stating the obvious, but before you start a business, or launch a new idea, it’s important to know how you’ll fund your project. According to AustraliaStartups.org, lack of funding is one of the most common reasons new businesses don't make it past the development stage. The same rule could arguably be applied to new projects you’d like to undertake, even as an established small business. What you’re about to start a business or you want help to grow your brand further, it pays to find out what funding may be available to you. What amount of funding is available in Australia? As reported by AustraliaStartups.org, as an Australian small business owner, you are in luck. Why?
Because the Australian government allocates billions of dollars each year to support small businesses across the country.
As a small business owner in Australia, you may also have access to hundreds of private funding sources, such as angel investors, venture capitalists and banks.
Funding may be granted in the following forms: grants loans tax credits, and private investments.
Who is eligible for grants in Australia?
Grants are often designed for specific industries and purposes, and many are suitable for small businesses.
Look for Government grants The federal and state governments of Australian offer over 500 grants and programs.
You can browse opportunities by visiting the grants and programs finder .

You can apply the following filters to the to the finder tool to help your search: Location Industry Business structure Support type Objectives Business stage Grant status Indigenous businesses The grants and programs finder also provides information on the kinds of support you may be eligible for.
Types of support state and federal governments may offer could include: Business advice and mentoring programs Funding Loans Sponsorships Subsidies and rebates Tax benefits.
Tip: Check your council website for funding opportunities that may be available in your local government area.

Search for grants that apply to specific industries and start-ups If you’re a start-up or are looking for support specific to your field, it’s worth searching for grants designed for your business stage or industry.
As defined by The Grants Hub , an auspice is an organisation who manages grant funding on your behalf.
